title: Psychosocial and Financial Impact of Dermatophytosis on Patients Attending a Tertiary Care Centre at Visakhapatnam: A Cross-Sectional Study
summary: A cross-sectional study at a tertiary care centre in Visakhapatnam examined the psychosocial and financial burden of dermatophytosis. Researchers assessed quality of life, stigma, mental health effects and direct out-of-pocket costs associated with recurrent fungal skin infections. Findings highlight substantial emotional distress, social withdrawal and financial strain for many patients, underlining the need for improved public awareness, accessible treatment, mental health screening and policies to reduce treatment costs and prevent chronicity.
content:
Background: Dermatophytosis (superficial fungal infections of the skin) has emerged as a persistent and recurrent problem in many communities. Beyond physical symptoms, these infections can impose significant psychosocial distress and financial strain on affected individuals. This study aimed to evaluate both the emotional and economic impacts experienced by patients attending a tertiary care centre in Visakhapatnam.

Methods: The investigation used a cross-sectional design among patients presenting with clinically and/or mycologically confirmed dermatophytosis. Data were collected using structured interviews and standardized questionnaires to capture quality of life measures, feelings of stigma, depressive or anxious symptoms, and the direct and indirect costs borne by patients. Costs included medication, clinic visits, investigations, and lost wages when applicable.

Findings: Many patients reported moderate to severe reductions in quality of life related to itching, visible lesions and sleep disturbance. Psychosocial effects commonly included embarrassment, avoidance of social situations, and concerns about transmission to family members. A subset of participants described symptoms consistent with anxiety or low mood linked to persistent or recurrent infection. Financially, out-of-pocket spending on multiple treatment attempts, over-the-counter remedies and repeat consultations accumulated over time, especially for patients with recurrent disease. Some patients delayed or discontinued care due to cost, contributing to prolonged illness.

Implications: The combined psychosocial and financial burdens of dermatophytosis suggest that medical management should extend beyond antifungal therapy. Clinicians and public health planners should consider integrating mental health screening, patient education to reduce stigma, and clearer treatment pathways to reduce unnecessary expenditures. Policies to improve access to affordable, evidence-based treatments and to reduce over-the-counter misuse of topical steroids and inappropriate medications could help limit chronicity and recurrence.

Conclusion: Dermatophytosis can have meaningful adverse effects on patients’ emotional well-being and household finances. Addressing the condition effectively requires coordinated clinical management, patient counselling, health education campaigns and policy measures to make appropriate treatment accessible and affordable for vulnerable populations in Visakhapatnam and similar settings.

- Embarrassment
- Avoidance of social situations
- Concerns about transmission to family members

- Out-of-pocket spending on multiple treatment attempts, over-the-counter remedies and repeat consultations accumulated over time, especially for patients with recurrent disease
- Some patients delayed or discontinued care due to cost, contributing to prolonged illness

## Implications

The combined psychosocial and financial burdens of dermatophytosis suggest that medical management should extend beyond antifungal therapy. Clinicians and public health planners should consider:
- Integrating mental health screening
- Providing patient education to reduce stigma
- Establishing clearer treatment pathways to reduce unnecessary expenditures
- Implementing policies to improve access to affordable, evidence-based treatments
- Reducing over-the-counter misuse of topical steroids and inappropriate medications to help limit chronicity and recurrence

Dermatophytosis can have meaningful adverse effects on patients’ emotional well-being and household finances. Addressing the condition effectively requires coordinated clinical management, patient counselling, health education campaigns and policy measures to make appropriate treatment accessible and affordable for vulnerable populations in Visakhapatnam and similar settings.
